extracted.intended_audience: sprout operations, food safety professionals, industry stakeholders, and commenters (interested public)
extracted.subtask_description: Notification of availability for FDA draft and final guidances giving recommended standards for growing, harvesting, packing, and holding sprouts for human consumption, including personnel, facilities, testing, and recordkeeping practices; also provides procedures for submitting comments to the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel Qualifications, Training, and Hygienic Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations on personnel qualifications, training, and hygienic practices consolidated into a standalone section in the draft guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the draft guidance, recommendations that were previously dispersed are consolidated into a single section entitled “Personnel Qualifications, Training, and Hygienic Practices” to present recommendations comprehensively and facilitate ease of reading. Stakeholders may comment on these consolidated recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buildings, Tools and Equipment (Equipment, Tools and Buildings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended standards and revisions for equipment, tools, and buildings used in sprout operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section has been revised to facilitate alignment with the recommendations in related guidances. The draft updates the January 2017 content (previously titled “Equipment, Tools and Buildings”) and stakeholders are invited to comment on these revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling and Testing of Spent Sprout Irrigation Water (or In-Process Sprouts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations and draft provisions on sampling and testing spent sprout irrigation water or in-process sprouts, reissued for additional comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA reissued this section in draft to receive additional comments and feedback from sprouting operations to inform ongoing FDA research. The agency specifically requests information about any testing that operations are currently doing for non-O157 Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC), including test kit names (as applicable). The final guidance removed language on voluntary periodic sampling and testing of sprouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning and Sanitizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarified recommendations regarding the frequency and practice of cleaning and sanitizing in sprout operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final guidance clarifies recommendations regarding the frequency of cleaning and sanitizing. (The document notes changes to improve clarity and removal of recommendations deemed impractical.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural Water in Sprouting Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations concerning the use, quality, and management of agricultural water in sprout production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final guidance includes a section addressing agricultural water specific to sprouting operations; stakeholders should follow or comment on recommended practices in this area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeds for Sprouting (including seed treatment and corrective actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations on seed for sprouting, including seed treatment options and corrective actions related to seed issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final guidance provides additional recommendations on seeds for sprouting, including seed treatment and corrective actions; the guidance also clarifies or adjusts prior recommendations from the January 2017 draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental monitoring recommendations including expectations for corrective actions after detection of Listeria spp. or Listeria monocytogenes in environmental samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final guidance clarifies FDA’s expectations for corrective actions after an operation detects Listeria spp. or Listeria monocytogenes in an environmental sample. Environmental monitoring remains a substantive element of the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and Information Collection (Paperwork Reduction Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordkeeping recommendations and notice that the guidance contains information collection provisions subject to OMB review under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections of information in 21 CFR part 112 have been approved under OMB control number 0910-0816. The guidance identifies recordkeeping expectations tied to PRA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Actions Following Pathogen Detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and clarified recommendations for corrective actions after detecting pathogens (e.g., Listeria spp., L. monocytogenes) in environmental samples or other monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final guidance clarifies expectations for corrective actions after an operation detects Listeria spp. or Listeria monocytogenes in an environmental sample; also addresses corrective actions related to seed issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance Non-Binding / Alternative Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that the guidance documents do not establish any rights and are not binding; alternative approaches may be used if they satisfy applicable statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issued consistent with good guidance practices (21 CFR 10.115). The guidance does not establish rights for any person and is not binding on FDA or the public; stakeholders can use alternative approaches if they satisfy statutory and regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of Voluntary Periodic Sampling Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Final guidance removes language that previously recommended voluntary periodic sampling and testing of sprouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency removed language on voluntary periodic sampling and testing of sprouts in the final guidance, reflecting stakeholder comment and practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Information on non-O157 STEC Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA expresses particular interest in receiving information about testing for non-O157 STEC in spent sprout irrigation water or in-process sprouts, including test kit names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FDA specifically requests stakeholders provide information on any testing currently performed for non-O157 STEC and the names of test kits used; responses will inform ongoing FDA research on this topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Submission Procedures and Confidential Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements for submitting electronic or written comments, and how to submit confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic comments: submit via https://www.regulations.gov per instructions; comments posted unchanged and may include identifying information unless excluded. Confidential comments: submit as written/paper submissions with two copies — one with claimed confidential information labeled “THIS DOCUMENT CONTAINS CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION” and a second redacted copy for public viewing; submit both to Dockets Management Staff. If you do not want your name/contact made public, place that information on the cover sheet and identify it as “confidential.” Information marked confidential will be handled under 21 CFR 10.20 and other disclosure law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket Access and Public Posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on how to access the docket, view background documents, and where submitted comments will be made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access the docket and read background documents or comments, go to https://www.regulations.gov and insert the docket number FDA-2017-D-0175; comments received will be placed in the docket and publicly viewable at regulations.gov or at the Docket office (address and phone provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Deadline and Timing for Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadline for submitting comments to ensure FDA considers them before finalizing the guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit electronic or written comments on the draft revised guidance by March 27, 2024 to ensure FDA considers your comment on the draft revised guidance before the agency begins work on the final version of the guidance. Comments may be submitted at any time, but submitting by the date ensures consideration prior to finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and Access to Guidance Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: How to obtain electronic or printed copies of the draft and final guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidances are available via FDA guidance web pages and regulations.gov; submit written requests for single printed copies to the Division of Produce Safety (contact/address provided) and include two self-addressed adhesive labels to assist processing. Use FDA website links provided to find the most current version of the guidance.
